content.comment_body: Hello, I am working on a project using a [article_no] [product_name]. I set up several display pages for diagnostics, with around 30 ON/OFF indicators across different pages to show marker states. Only one page is active at a time, managed through my software. Everything works fine for up to 20 indicators, but adding more causes some (seemingly random) indicators to disappear from the [product_name] display. In simulation, all indicators show correctly. I couldn't determine the exact maximum number allowed; for instance, adding four more results in an indicator vanishing from another page. Thank you.
Could you please upload your program as a Zip file?

I checked the online help, which notes that a program supports up to 40 I/O status names, with no more than eight per message text. I created a small program and confirmed inserting I/O status names in five message texts. Using your program, I also managed 40 status names. Which firmware version does your [product_name] have? Which [product_name] version are you using?

I tested your program on actual [product_name] hardware and now see the issue you described. For example, with message text SF012, a status name is inserted in the fourth line to display the status of input I11. It appears in the simulation but not on the real hardware. Moving the status name to the sixth line yields the same result. Adding a new status name to the fourth line, however, does display correctly, even after deleting the one in the sixth line. The new status name remains visible, which is very odd. I'm not sure why this occurs. I've attached the modified program and screenshots showing the order of changes.
I'm using [product_name] [version_no]. I am downloading [product_name] [version_no] SP1 because there may be some bugs—I'll try to see if this fixes the issue.

I installed the [version_no] update, but the issue persists. After adding all indicators needed, I noticed two that aren't displayed. Using your suggested method, I could restore one missing indicator, but the other still won't show. Next, I'll try updating the firmware on my [product_name].
Please upload your currently adjusted program showing the error and describe which message text (SFxxx) and line number. I may be able to help.
The indicator not displayed is in message SF013, input I15. Thank you.

I made further progress. Trying the same approach as with SF012—without success—I noticed the same outcome as you. Then I deleted SF013 and created a new message text, assigning the same address (SF013) and inserting texts and status names before transferring to the [product_name]. Things got worse this time: now the status names for I13 and I16 were missing, while I14 and I15 were okay. Then, I first created a new message text (SF044), then deleted the old SF013, inserted texts and status names, and transferred to the [product_name]. Everything worked flawlessly. It's all very puzzling.

I followed your instructions and now everything works properly in my project. It's odd, but the issue is resolved. Since you seem very knowledgeable, do you know how to report this bug to [company_name]? Thank you.

I tested the latest version of the file (Opera de presa). Since I can only modify I1 to I6, I changed the inputs to I1 to I4 in SF012. It works in my [product_name] [version_no]. Text and statuses for I1 to I4 display as expected. Tip: For testing, I set EN of SF012 to high so the message text is always visible, regardless of the rest of the program.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members have discovered that ON/OFF indicator statuses displayed on diagnostic pages behave differently between the [product_name] simulator and its actual hardware. Exceeding a certain number of displayed statuses leads to disappearance of some indicators on physical devices, although the simulation works as planned. Efforts to rearrange, delete, or recreate message texts show inconsistent results, and neither updating the configuration software nor firmware reliably resolves the problem. The root cause seems to be related to firmware or project file handling.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect all configured ON/OFF status indicators to be displayed reliably on the hardware, mirroring simulation behavior, no matter the total count or page location.
